import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture

The Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture states that a group $G$ with cohomological dimension $2$ also has a
$2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$.

Here the *cohomological dimension* $\operatorname{cd}(G)$ is the projective dimension of the
trivial module $\mathbb{Z}$ over the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$, i.e. the supremum of
the $n$ such that $H^n(G, M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module $M$. An Eilenberg–MacLane
space $K(G, 1)$ is a path-connected space with $\pi_1 \cong G$ and $\pi_n = 0$ for all $n \geq 2$.
The conjecture asks for such a space that is moreover a CW complex of dimension $2$.

The conjecture was formulated by Eilenberg and Ganea in 1957. It is known that for $n \neq 2$ a
group of cohomological dimension $n$ has an $n$-dimensional $K(G, 1)$, and that a group of
cohomological dimension $2$ has a $3$-dimensional $K(G, 1)$. Bestvina and Brady (1997) showed that
the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture and the Whitehead asphericity conjecture cannot both be true.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilenberg%E2%80%93Ganea_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [EG57] Eilenberg, Samuel; Ganea, Tudor. *On the Lusternik–Schnirelmann category of abstract
  groups.* Annals of Mathematics 65 (1957), 517–518.
- [BB97] Bestvina, Mladen; Brady, Noel. *Morse theory and finiteness properties of groups.*
  Inventiones Mathematicae 129 (1997), 445–470.
-/

namespace EilenbergGaneaConjecture

open CategoryTheory Topology

/-- The (integral) cohomological dimension $\operatorname{cd}(G)$ of a group `G`: the projective
dimension of `ℤ` with the trivial `G`-action in the abelian category `Rep ℤ G` of `ℤ[G]`-modules.
Since `Extⁱ(ℤ, M)` in `Rep ℤ G` is the group cohomology `Hⁱ(G, M)`, this is the supremum of the
`n` such that `Hⁿ(G, M) ≠ 0` for some `ℤ[G]`-module `M` (it is `⊤` if no such supremum exists). -/
noncomputable def cohomologicalDimension (G : Type) [Group G] : WithBot ℕ∞ :=
  projectiveDimension (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ)

/-- The trivial group has cohomological dimension `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20 55]
theorem cohomologicalDimension_eq_zero_of_subsingleton (G : Type) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    cohomologicalDimension G = 0 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact_mod_cast (projectiveDimension_le_iff (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ) 0).2 inferInstance
  · have h := (projectiveDimension_ge_iff (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ) 0).2 ?_
    · exact_mod_cast h
    rw [hasProjectiveDimensionLT_zero_iff_isZero]
    intro h
    have := congr_arg (fun f : Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ ⟶ Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ => f.hom.hom (1 : ℤ))
      (h.eq_of_src (𝟙 _) 0)
    simp at this

/-- A topological space `X` is an Eilenberg–MacLane space `K(G, 1)` for the group `G` if it is
path-connected and, for every basepoint `x`, the fundamental group `π₁(X, x)` is isomorphic to `G`
and the higher homotopy groups `πₙ(X, x)`, `n ≥ 2`, are trivial. -/
def IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace (G : Type) [Group G] (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  PathConnectedSpace X ∧
    ∀ x : X, Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G) ∧ ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → Subsingleton (π_ n X x)

/-- A Hausdorff topological space `X` is a CW complex of dimension `d` if it carries a CW structure
with at least one `d`-cell and no cells of dimension greater than `d`. -/
def IsCWComplexOfDimension (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  T2Space X ∧ ∃ _ : CWComplex (Set.univ : Set X),
    Nonempty (RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set X) d) ∧
      ∀ n, d < n → IsEmpty (RelCWComplex.cell (Set.univ : Set X) n)

/-- **Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture.** A group $G$ with cohomological dimension $2$ also has a
$2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$: there is a $2$-dimensional CW complex $X$
that is path-connected with $\pi_1(X) \cong G$ and $\pi_n(X) = 0$ for all $n \geq 2$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20 55 57]
theorem eilenberg_ganea_conjecture (G : Type) [Group G] (hG : cohomologicalDimension G = 2) :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X),
      IsCWComplexOfDimension X 2 ∧ IsEilenbergMacLaneSpace G X := by
  sorry

end EilenbergGaneaConjecture

$2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$, i.e. a $2$-dimensional aspherical CW complex
with fundamental group $G$.

The (integral) cohomological dimension of $G$ is
$$\operatorname{cd}(G) = \sup \{ n \mid H^n(G; M) \neq 0 \text{ for some } G\text{-module } M \}.$$
For $n \neq 2$, a group of cohomological dimension $n$ has an $n$-dimensional $K(G, 1)$, and a
group of cohomological dimension $2$ has a $3$-dimensional $K(G, 1)$. Bestvina and Brady showed
that the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture and the Whitehead asphericity conjecture cannot both be true.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilenberg%E2%80%93Ganea_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, list of unsolved problems in

- [EG57] Eilenberg, Samuel; Ganea, Tudor. "On the Lusternik–Schnirelmann category of abstract
  groups." Annals of Mathematics 65 (1957), 517–518. https://doi.org/10.2307/1970062
- [BB97] Bestvina, Mladen; Brady, Noel. "Morse theory and finiteness properties of groups."
  Inventiones Mathematicae 129 (1997), 445–470. https://doi.org/10.1007/s002220050168
-/

namespace EilenbergGaneaConjecture

open CategoryTheory Set Topology

/-- The (integral) cohomological dimension of a group `G`, as an element of `ℕ∞`: the supremum
of the natural numbers `n` such that the group cohomology `Hⁿ(G; M)` is nonzero for some
`G`-module `M` (i.e. some `ℤ`-linear representation `M : Rep ℤ G`). It is `⊤` when
`Hⁿ(G; M)` is nonzero for infinitely many `n` (e.g. when `G` has torsion). -/
noncomputable def cohomologicalDimension (G : Type) [Group G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : ∃ M : Rep ℤ G, ¬ Limits.IsZero (groupCohomology M n)), (n : ℕ∞)

/-- The cohomological dimension of `G` is at most `n` if and only if `Hᵏ(G; M) = 0` for every
`G`-module `M` and every `k > n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem cohomologicalDimension_le_iff (G : Type) [Group G] (n : ℕ) :
    cohomologicalDimension G ≤ n ↔
      ∀ (M : Rep ℤ G) (k : ℕ), n < k → Limits.IsZero (groupCohomology M k) := by
  simp only [cohomologicalDimension, iSup_le_iff, Nat.cast_le]
  refine ⟨fun h M k hk => ?_, fun h k ⟨M, hM⟩ => ?_⟩
  · by_contra hM
    exact (h k ⟨M, hM⟩).not_gt hk
  · by_contra hk
    exact hM (h M k (not_le.mp hk))

/-- The trivial group has cohomological dimension `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem cohomologicalDimension_eq_zero_of_subsingleton (G : Type) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    cohomologicalDimension G = 0 := by
  rw [← nonpos_iff_eq_zero, ← Nat.cast_zero, cohomologicalDimension_le_iff]
  intro M k hk
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero hk.ne'
  exact isZero_groupCohomology_succ_of_subsingleton M k

/-- **Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture.** If a group $G$ has cohomological dimension $2$, then $G$ has a
$2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G, 1)$: there is a (Hausdorff) CW complex $X$ with no
cells of dimension greater than $2$ (and at least one $2$-cell) which is path-connected, has
fundamental group isomorphic to $G$, and has trivial homotopy groups $\pi_n(X)$ for all $n \geq 2$.

Since $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$ forces every $K(G, 1)$ to have dimension at least $2$, the
requirement that $X$ has a $2$-cell is automatic; it is included so that $X$ is literally
$2$-dimensional. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20 55]
theorem eilenberg_ganea_conjecture (G : Type) [Group G] (hG : cohomologicalDimension G = 2) :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X) (_ : T2Space X) (_ : CWComplex (univ : Set X)),
      (∀ n > 2, IsEmpty (RelCWComplex.cell (univ : Set X) n)) ∧
        Nonempty (RelCWComplex.cell (univ : Set X) 2) ∧
        PathConnectedSpace X ∧
        ∃ x : X, Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G) ∧
          ∀ n ≥ 2, Subsingleton (π_ n X x) := by
  sorry

end EilenbergGaneaConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture

The Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture concerns the relation between the integral cohomological dimension
of a group and the minimum dimension of its Eilenberg–MacLane spaces.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilenberg%E2%80%93Ganea_conjecture)
-/

namespace EilenbergGaneaConjecture

open Topology

/--
The Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture: every group $G$ of integral cohomological dimension $2$ has a
$2$-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G,1)$. Here integral cohomological dimension is the
projective dimension of the trivial $G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$. The conclusion gives a path-connected
Hausdorff CW complex with fundamental group $G$, at least one $2$-cell and no cells above
dimension $2$, and trivial homotopy groups in every dimension at least $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 55]
theorem eilenberg_ganea_conjecture :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      CategoryTheory.projectiveDimension (Rep.trivial ℤ G ℤ) = 2 →
        ∃ (X : Type) (τ : TopologicalSpace X) (x : X)
          (cw : @CWComplex X τ Set.univ),
          letI := τ
          letI := cw
          T2Space X ∧ PathConnectedSpace X ∧
            Nonempty (FundamentalGroup X x ≃* G) ∧
            Nonempty (@Topology.CWComplex.cell X τ Set.univ cw 2) ∧
            (∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → IsEmpty (@Topology.CWComplex.cell X τ Set.univ cw n)) ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup.Pi n X x) := by
  sorry

end EilenbergGaneaConjecture

Expanded the terse phrase “a 2-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space K(G,1)” using the background article and decomposition notes as a path-connected Hausdorff CW complex whose fundamental group is isomorphic to G and whose homotopy groups in every degree n ≥ 2 are trivial.

Modeled trivial higher homotopy groups by `Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup.Pi n X x)`; Mathlib supplies an `Inhabited` instance for every such homotopy group, so this expresses the trivial group/type rather than possible emptiness.
